one_liner: Branchless public-domain 2D/3D Hilbert index encode/decode; a Rust port encodes about 5.4x faster than the classic rotation loop.
what_it_does: A single C++ file with four functions: hilbertXYToIndex(n, x, y) and hilbertIndexToXY(n, i, x, y) for 2D curves of order n up to 16 (32-bit index), plus mortonToHilbert3D and hilbertToMorton3D, which convert a 3D Morton (Z-order) code of up to 10 levels into a Hilbert code and back. It produces the same index as the textbook xy2d/d2xy loop, so it can replace that loop in code that sorts points or boxes along a Hilbert curve, such as packed R-tree bulk loading. There is no header, namespace, build system or test suite.
how_it_is_fast: The 2D encoder runs the per-level quadrant-rotation state machine as a parallel prefix scan over all 16 levels at once, using log2(16) = 4 rounds of XOR/AND/shift on bit-sliced state words, then bit-interleaves the result. The decoder uses the same prefix-scan idea, so both directions run in constant time with no branches and no memory lookups. Because nothing depends on the data, a compiler can auto-vectorize a loop over many points. The 3D path is different: it walks multiplication tables of the alternating group A4 (pre-combined with the Morton-to-Hilbert mapping), one 3-bit digit per step.
when_to_use: Bulk-loading a packed Hilbert R-tree or sorting items by Hilbert key, with coordinates quantized to 16 bits per axis (the Flatbush and static_aabb2d_index approach; both embed ports of this exact function).

Encoding large arrays of independent points, where the branchless body auto-vectorizes. In the port's benchmark this was 5.4x faster than the rotation loop and 3.5x faster than the fast_hilbert crate.
When you need decode (index to x, y) as well as encode, with run time that does not depend on the data.
3D Hilbert ordering when you already have Morton codes of up to 30 bits (10 levels per axis), for example from a pdep- or magic-bits interleaver.
When you want public-domain code to vendor; JS and Rust ports already exist.
when_not_to_use: Coordinates wider than 16 bits per axis in 2D, or 10 bits in 3D: every index is 32-bit, and nothing here produces 64-bit codes.
Single calls in a dependent latency chain: the port's notes say its table-driven LUT encoder wins there. The 5.4x figure is batch throughput only.
When Z-order is good enough: in the same port benchmark, Morton encoding took 47 us per 100k points against 185 us for this encoder.
When you need a maintained, packaged library with tests, or more than three dimensions, or other curve variants: this is four commits from 2016 with none of these.
3D throughput-critical code: the 3D functions are a serial table walk, take Morton codes rather than x/y/z, and no one has benchmarked them.

integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (uses <cstdint> fixed-width types; no intrinsics or other language features)
integration.platforms: any (portable 32-bit unsigned integer arithmetic, no SIMD intrinsics or platform code)
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. From the code: pure functions plus read-only static tables, so concurrent calls are safe.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it computes the same index as the classic xy2d/d2xy rotation loop (checked against the port's loop_rotation), but it takes the curve order n in bits, not the grid side length, and it is capped at n = 16

gotchas: No input checking. n must be 1 to 16: n = 0 shifts a uint32_t by 32, which is undefined behavior, and n > 16 gives a negative shift count. Coordinates must also be below 2^n. They are not masked, so an out-of-range coordinate silently returns a different, in-range index. In a Python transcription at n = 4, (x=17, y=3) gave index 12, while (x=1, y=3) gave 6.

The file defines external-linkage free functions with generic names (interleave, deinterleave, prefixScan, descan, transformCurve) in the global namespace, and there is no header. Compiling it into more than one translation unit, or next to other bit-twiddling helpers, causes duplicate-symbol link errors. Wrap it in a namespace and mark the functions inline or static when vendoring.
The 3D functions convert between Morton and Hilbert codes, not x/y/z, so you need your own 3D bit interleaver. Use bits of 10 or less: at 11, the code needs 33 bits and the top digit is truncated.

No correctness bug was found. A Python transcription of the C++ was checked exhaustively for 2D orders 1 to 8 and 3D levels 1 to 5, plus 200,000 random 2D points at order 16 and 100,000 random 3D codes at 10 levels. Results: bijective, consecutive indices are unit steps apart, encode/decode round-trips, and 2D output equals the classic rotation loop. The decoder and the 3D functions have never been benchmarked by anyone.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Flatbush already contains a JS port of this exact function, credited in its index.js, for its packed Hilbert R-tree. Pick this repo when you want the raw encoder/decoder in C++ to build your own packed index or sort keys, not a finished spatial index such as Flatbush, KDBush or nanoflann.
verified_claims_summary: The repo has no numbers. The only measurement is of Filyus/packed_spatial_index's magic_bits, a line-for-line Rust port of hilbertXYToIndex fixed at order 16. It encoded 100,000 random (u16, u16) points in 185 us, against 998 us for the classic loop_rotation encoder (about 5.4x, derived from page data) and 644 us for fast_hilbert 2.1.0. The run used Criterion with LTO and codegen-units = 1, on a Ryzen AI 7 350 with the thread pinned to one core; the rustc version and target-cpu are not stated. The harness looks fair: all encoders run the same loop with black_box only on the buffers, and their outputs are identical. But the ratio mixes the algorithm with auto-vectorization, which the branchy baseline cannot get.
status_note: Abandoned since 2016-09-18 (4 commits, no pull requests, two closed 2018 issues), and the author's explanation posts on threadlocalmutex.com no longer resolve. Still copyable: about 150 lines released into the public domain by an informal README statement (no LICENSE file, no patent grant), with no correctness bug found and widely re-ported (Flatbush, static_aabb2d_index, packed_spatial_index).
